title: Markets: Sunday 8 November

morning.session_note: Weekend edition · what's new since Saturday, with the week ahead
summary: President Trump said US forces carried out "minor" strikes on Iranian air defences on Friday evening as Iranian media reported explosions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, while Qatar pressed a plan that would reopen the strait in return for IAEA visits and a partial unfreezing of Iranian assets ([AP via NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/us-military-carries-new-targeted-strikes-iran-rcna607969), [Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/07/strait-of-hormuz-qatar-plan-iran-nuclear-inspections), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-speaks-strait-hormuz-11-07-26)). Brent futures closed Friday at US$98.32 (unchanged on the day, −16.4% for the week) in our data.

Friday's US equity closes are now in our dashboard after Saturday's issue still carried Thursday's session: the S&P 500 finished at 7,376.9 (+0.3% Friday, −2.7% week) and the Nasdaq at 24,579.4 (+1.1%, −3.4% week), with the VIX at 25.64 (−2.54 pts Friday). CME FedWatch put a 25 bp Fed rise on 9 December at 76.8% after Friday's payrolls print ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/07/odds-of-a-december-rate-hike-jump-to-77-after-a-blowout-jobs-report/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/jobs-report-october-2026.html)).

This week: China October CPI/PPI early Monday Sydney time; RBA Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter speaks Monday; Westpac–Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment and the NAB business survey Tuesday; US October CPI Tuesday evening Sydney time; ANZ's full-year result Monday and CBA's first-quarter update Wednesday; Flight Centre's AGM Wednesday ([CommSec](https://www.commsec.com.au/content/dam/EN/ResearchNews/2026Reports/November/ECO_Insights_091126-Week-Ahead.pdf)).

cards.headline: Qeshm "minor" strikes and a Qatar Hormuz reopen plan
cards.takeaway: Trump described limited Friday strikes on Iranian air defences while Qatar floated a sequenced deal to reopen the strait; oil stayed near US$98 after its steep weekly fall.
cards.key_figure: Brent futures US$98.32 (flat Fri, −16.4% week); UKMTO: Hormuz traffic ~65% below pre-conflict
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday covered the week's tanker attacks and mediation in outline. New: Trump's Friday-evening "minor strikes" remarks and Iranian reports of Qeshm explosions; the Guardian's detail of Qatar's reopen-for-inspections proposal; UKMTO's weekly transit count; a Saturday IRGC mine-strike claim on a dark tanker.
cards.what_happened: President Trump told reporters on Friday evening that US forces had carried out "minor" strikes that knocked out an Iranian anti-aircraft device "in about 15 minutes, maybe five," as Iranian state media reported two projectiles hitting the Suza area of Qeshm Island ([AP via NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/us-military-carries-new-targeted-strikes-iran-rcna607969), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-speaks-strait-hormuz-11-07-26), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/07/us-launches-new-targeted-strikes-on-iran-as-trump-claims-progress-in-talks-with-tehran)). He also said the US was "dealing with" Iran and that "they want to make a deal," while Qatar denied reports that talks had collapsed ([Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/07/us-launches-new-targeted-strikes-on-iran-as-trump-claims-progress-in-talks-with-tehran)). Under Qatar's proposal as set out in weekend reporting, Washington would lift its Hormuz naval blockade and release a portion of about US$8bn in frozen Iranian assets, with Iran allowing IAEA visits to bombed nuclear sites and reopening the strait on day two via an Oman-agreed route lodged with the IMO ([Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/07/strait-of-hormuz-qatar-plan-iran-nuclear-inspections)). UKMTO said at least 11 ships were attacked in and around Hormuz in the week to 6 November, with three sunk, and counted 170 outbound and 155 inbound transits — about 65% below pre-conflict levels ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/7/qeshm-island-and-hormuz-hit-as-mediators-try-to-prevent-us-iran-escalation)). Iran's navy said on Saturday that a tanker with its transponder off caught fire after hitting a mine in the eastern strait; Washington says mines have been cleared ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/7/qeshm-island-and-hormuz-hit-as-mediators-try-to-prevent-us-iran-escalation)). Our futures feed closed Friday at US$98.32 (flat on the day, −16.4% for the week). FRED spot Brent, lagged to 3 November, was US$107.03 (−13.1% on the prior week in our data).
cards.why_it_matters: Hormuz is the main oil-price channel into Australian fuel costs and the inflation path the RBA cited when it raised the cash rate to 4.85% on 3 November ([RBA](https://www.rba.gov.au/media-releases/2026/mr-26-30.html)). A sequenced reopen would ease that pressure; further strikes or mine incidents would reverse last week's price fall.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: Brent futures 98.32 (flat day, −16.4% week, session 6 Nov); Brent spot 107.03 as at 3 Nov (FRED, −13.1% week). Iron ore unavailable.

competing_views.view: Told investors Friday her desk was struck by the divergence between deepening escalation concerns in the Gulf and "headline driven off-ramp optimism" among market participants thousands of miles away.

competing_views.who: Dr Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, UAE Federal National Council
competing_views.view: Said he sees "some progress" in Qatari-mediated talks and is "a little bit optimistic," while still not excluding renewed war and saying the UAE plans for the worst.

cards.headline: Friday's US rebound is now in the dashboard ahead of CPI
cards.takeaway: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq recovered part of Thursday's AI-led fall on Friday; October CPI on Tuesday is the next Fed pricing test.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday's issue still stamped the 5 November US equity session and cited Friday's rebound only from secondary reporting. New: Friday closes are now in our snapshot, plus weekend FedWatch and Mary Daly commentary into the CPI week.
cards.what_happened: Our US equity feed now shows the 6 November close: the S&P 500 at 7,376.9 (+0.3% on the day, −2.7% for the week) and the Nasdaq at 24,579.4 (+1.1%, −3.4% week), after Thursday's AI-led selloff had taken the S&P 500 down 4.4% on the 5 November session in Saturday's data. The VIX closed at 25.64 (−2.54 pts Friday, +6.22 pts for the week). CME FedWatch put the chance of a 25 bp rise at the 9 December FOMC at 76.8% after Friday's payrolls print, up from 66.9% a week earlier, according to 24/7 Wall St. ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/07/odds-of-a-december-rate-hike-jump-to-77-after-a-blowout-jobs-report/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/jobs-report-october-2026.html)). San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said Friday the Fed will likely have to tighten further to bring down inflation that is still too high, without giving timing or size ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/07/odds-of-a-december-rate-hike-jump-to-77-after-a-blowout-jobs-report/)). CME Group flagged October CPI on Tuesday as the week's main US data release, with core CPI expected +0.2% m/m and headline +0.3% m/m ([CME Group](https://www.cmegroup.com/videos/2026/11/07/october-u-s-cpi-report-arrives-to-set-december-fed-expectations.html)).
cards.why_it_matters: Friday's partial rebound does not reverse the week's AI and chip drawdown. CPI will test whether December Fed hike odds stay near the high 70s, which feeds into ASX rate-sensitive sectors and the Australian dollar when cash markets reopen.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard (US session 6 Nov): S&P 500 7,376.9 (+0.3% day, −2.7% week); Nasdaq 24,579.4 (+1.1% day, −3.4% week); VIX 25.64 (−2.54 pts day, +6.22 pts week).

competing_views.who: Mary Daly, San Francisco Fed President
competing_views.view: Said the Fed will likely have to tighten further against still-high inflation, preferring a deliberate, gradual approach, and called the technology-stock revaluation painful but measured.

cards.headline: US yields edged up Friday after payrolls; CPI is next
cards.takeaway: The US 2-year yield rose 5 bp on Friday as December Fed hike odds reset higher; Australian yields remain lagged to 4 November in our feed.
cards.key_figure: US 10Y 4.86% (−8 bp week); US 2Y 4.51% (−5 bp week); AU 10Y 5.08% (−13 bp week, as at 4 Nov)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday used the 5 November US yield session. New: Friday's +2 bp (10-year) and +5 bp (2-year) moves are now in the snapshot, alongside weekend FedWatch detail into the CPI print.
cards.what_happened: In our data the US 10-year yield closed 6 November at 4.86% (+2 bp on the day, −8 bp for the week) and the 2-year at 4.51% (+5 bp day, −5 bp week), as short-end yields rose with Friday's strong payrolls print ([24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/07/odds-of-a-december-rate-hike-jump-to-77-after-a-blowout-jobs-report/)). Australia's RBA-published yields through 4 November show the 10-year at 5.08% (−13 bp week) and the 2-year at 4.83% (−12 bp week), leaving the 10-year–2-year curve at +26 bp. CME FedWatch put a December quarter-point hike at 76.8% after payrolls ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/jobs-report-october-2026.html), [24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/07/odds-of-a-december-rate-hike-jump-to-77-after-a-blowout-jobs-report/)). RBA Rate Watch, modelling ASX futures, still showed an 11.3% chance of a December RBA rise and a 78.4% hold at its Friday 2:26pm AEDT stamp ([RBA Rate Watch](https://rbaratewatch.com/)).
cards.why_it_matters: A firmer front-end US curve after payrolls raises the bar for equities into CPI. In Australia, futures still lean toward a December hold after the 3 November hike, so Hunter's Monday remarks and Tuesday's confidence surveys are the near-term local signals.
cards.market_reaction: Dashboard: US 10Y 4.86% (+2 bp day, −8 bp week); US 2Y 4.51% (+5 bp day, −5 bp week); AU 10Y 5.08% and AU 2Y 4.83% as at 4 Nov (RBA, lagged); curve +26 bp.
cards.what_to_watch: US CPI Tuesday; Fed speakers; RBA Hunter Monday.

cards.headline: Democrats say ending the Iran war will be an early priority
cards.takeaway: Incoming majorities plan war-powers and funding pressure from January; Trump can still act before then, and analysts say Gulf escalation risk remains high.
cards.key_figure: Government funding expires 11 Dec; Democrats take Congress in January
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday covered the midterm result and Vance linking the loss to the war. New: weekend reporting on Democratic legislative plans, the Dec. 11 funding leverage, and CNBC's escalation-risk wrap with Trump's "locked and loaded" remarks.
cards.what_happened: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said Democrats will "get out of the gate fast" on healthcare and legislation to stop the war with Iran after taking majorities ([AP](https://apnews.com/article/democrats-house-majority-iran-war-healthcare-tariffs-0658bbfc51d2bc23331714377cddb0d2)). Democrats plan a war-powers resolution but are not sworn in until January, and Trump can veto such a measure; RBC's Helima Croft pointed to the 11 December government-funding deadline as the main purse leverage once Democrats hold both chambers ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/07/iran-war-midterm-election-oil-price-trump.html)). Trump told reporters on Thursday he would decide soon on whether to attack Iran again, saying he would "rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible but maybe I'll have to" and that forces were "locked and loaded" ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/07/iran-war-midterm-election-oil-price-trump.html)). On Friday he described limited strikes as "minor" while saying progress was being made in talks ([AP via NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/us-military-carries-new-targeted-strikes-iran-rcna607969)).
cards.why_it_matters: Last week's oil drop coincided with midterm hopes of a diplomatic off-ramp. The political constraint on the White House is delayed until January, so the near-term oil path still turns on military and mediation headlines before Democrats sit.

competing_views.view: Said on Thursday he was "locked and loaded" on further Iran action if needed, and on Friday that the US was "dealing with" Iran and that "they want to make a deal."

competing_views.who: Hakeem Jeffries, House Democratic leader (via AP)
competing_views.view: Said Democrats will move quickly once they hold the majority, including on legislation aimed at ending the Iran war.

cards.what_to_watch: Any war-powers draft text; December funding talks; further White House decisions on strikes.

cards.headline: Iran lifted its stated missile-range limit as mediators kept calling
cards.takeaway: IRGC said a self-imposed ballistic-missile range limit is lifted; Araghchi spoke to a dozen foreign ministers; CENTCOM offered a nuclear tip reward.
cards.key_figure: UKMTO: 88 projectile strikes since early July (most unreported)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday noted continued mediation and tanker hits. New: Saturday IRGC range-limit remarks; Araghchi's 12-minister outreach; CENTCOM's US$20m Rewards for Justice post; Erdoğan–Trump diplomacy call reporting.
cards.what_happened: IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said on Saturday that a long-standing self-imposed ballistic-missile range limit of about 2,000 km had been "lifted for us," without saying Iran already had longer-range missiles ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/7/qeshm-island-and-hormuz-hit-as-mediators-try-to-prevent-us-iran-escalation), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-speaks-strait-hormuz-11-07-26)). Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he held talks with 12 foreign ministers over 48 hours, restating seven demands to reopen Hormuz and calling for regional security arrangements without "superregional" powers ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/7/qeshm-island-and-hormuz-hit-as-mediators-try-to-prevent-us-iran-escalation)). US Central Command said late Friday the US was offering a reward of up to US$20 million for information on Iran's nuclear programme ([AP via NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/us-military-carries-new-targeted-strikes-iran-rcna607969), [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-speaks-strait-hormuz-11-07-26)). Turkish President Erdoğan told Trump the US–Iran conflict should be resolved through diplomacy, according to a statement from Erdoğan's office reported by Reuters and carried in weekend updates ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-speaks-strait-hormuz-11-07-26)). A Saudi-led coalition said early Saturday that air defences intercepted a Houthi cruise missile toward the Riyadh area ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-speaks-strait-hormuz-11-07-26)).
cards.why_it_matters: Harder Iranian military rhetoric and a CENTCOM tip reward sit alongside mediation calls, which is the same two-track pattern that has kept oil volatile. Regional missile intercepts keep Gulf risk premia in freight and insurance even when futures prices fall on diplomacy hopes.

competing_views.who: Trita Parsi, Quincy Institute (via Al Jazeera)
competing_views.view: Said three post-midterm factors raise near-term war risk unless talks break through: the political cost of high fuel prices has already been paid, hawks face a January congressional constraint, and a "vengeance" element after the midterm loss.
Sees an 80% chance that fighting will resume as diplomacy stalls.

cards.what_to_watch: Further IRGC statements, mediator readouts, and any CENTCOM operational updates.

cards.headline: Russian diesel tankers diverted as US legal risk stays high
cards.takeaway: Zero Russian diesel has reached the US under the Trump–Putin deal; tankers changed course as Congress's import ban and state warnings deter buyers.
cards.key_figure: US retail diesel still elevated (~US$6.21/gal AAA, as reported Sat)
cards.new_since_last_issue: Not covered on Saturday. New weekend reporting on diverted tankers and the clash between Treasury's temporary exemption and Congress's ban.
cards.what_happened: At least three tankers carrying Russian diesel toward the United States changed course, with none of the promised cargo yet reaching US ports nearly a month after President Trump said Russia would release diesel stocks to US and global markets, according to weekend reporting. Kpler and MarineTraffic data cited in the piece showed vessels heading toward Brazil, the Mediterranean, or "for orders." The Treasury's OFAC issued a temporary sanctions exemption, while Congress's ban on Russian energy imports remains in place; New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill told port operators to turn ships away ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/7/why-are-oil-traders-refusing-to-buy-russian-diesel-after-trump-putin-deal)). Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said "all the diesel will find its buyers"; Kirill Dmitriev called diversion reports "fake" ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/7/why-are-oil-traders-refusing-to-buy-russian-diesel-after-trump-putin-deal)). AAA data showed the US regular gasoline average had fallen nearly 15 cents over the week to about US$4.04 a gallon as of Saturday, with diesel at US$6.21 ([Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-speaks-strait-hormuz-11-07-26)).
cards.why_it_matters: The diesel deal was marketed as a supply relief valve while Hormuz stays restricted. If cargoes cannot land in the US, the inflation channel from middle-distillate prices stays open even as crude futures fall on Iran diplomacy hopes.

competing_views.who: Matt Smith, Kpler (via AP, as reported by Al Jazeera)
competing_views.view: Said there is clear hesitancy bringing barrels onshore because of the legal implications, and cargoes may not discharge on the US Atlantic coast.
Said all the diesel will find its buyers.

cards.what_to_watch: Whether any tanker discharges in the US; further OFAC or congressional statements.

cards.headline: Gold held weekly gains into the CPI week
cards.takeaway: Gold futures closed Friday at 4,074.9, down on the day but up 4.5% for the week as the dollar and yields had eased earlier after the midterms.
cards.new_since_last_issue: Saturday used a 4,071.7 Friday print from an earlier feed stamp. New: our snapshot now shows 4,074.9 for the 6 November session, and the week ahead turns on CPI rather than midterm day-two flows.
cards.what_happened: Gold futures in our data closed at 4,074.9 on 6 November (−0.9% on the day, +4.5% for the week). Midweek, spot and futures rose as the dollar and Treasury yields eased and oil fell after the midterms; Friday's payrolls print then lifted short-end yields ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/05/gold-hits-two-week-high-as-dollar-yields-ease-after-us-midterms.html), [24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/07/odds-of-a-december-rate-hike-jump-to-77-after-a-blowout-jobs-report/)).
cards.why_it_matters: Midweek reporting tied gold's rise to a softer dollar, lower yields and weaker oil after the midterms; a hot CPI print that lifts December Fed odds further would work against that. On the ASX, gold miners were among last week's relative winners in Saturday's wrap.
cards.what_to_watch: US CPI Tuesday and whether post-midterm dollar softness holds.
